reference: Published write target-directory/banner-suppression and careful-byte-output contracts, independently encoded literal byte strings checked using Python. The receiver is an ordinary relative private file, with forced mode gating. No GNU terminal-delivery parity or live terminal claim is made.
coverage: Loadable registration as a Bash builtin, checked with type -t without invoking write.
Help synopsis and documented message/target behavior, checked through Bash help without invoking write.
Contract: private-file argument/stdin delivery, careful-byte escaping and forced permission/missing-target errors; PTY/banner/EOF/fault behavior remains deferred.
Executed joined arguments, binary stdin, newline conversion, control/high-byte rendering and permission/missing-target errors through private regular-file receivers.
exclusions: Real PTY banners, EOF/session semantics, system recipients and injected write faults remain deferred; regular-file capture only qualifies the documented byte transformation and append behavior.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t classifies an enabled shell builtin as builtin; this confirms write registration without calling the loadable.

Check that Bash help exposes the documented synopsis, command purpose, EOF marker, and target-directory environment knob. The assertions are grounded in the builtin help contract and do not invoke write.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help write)
[[ $help_text == *'write TTY [MSG ...]'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'Send a message to a single terminal (write(1)).'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'trailing EOF marker.'* ]]
[[ $help_text == *'BASHWALL_DEV_DIR'* ]]
printf 'write help metadata present\n'

cases.purpose: Use the documented target-directory override and banner suppression to append joined arguments to a private regular-file receiver; no terminal recipient is addressed.
cases.script:
export BASHWALL_DEV_DIR=. BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 BASHWALL_FORCE_MESG=1
umask 000
printf 'prefix:' > receiver
chmod 666 receiver
write receiver hello "two words"
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
assert Path("receiver").read_bytes() == b"prefix:hello two words\r\n"
print("argument bytes appended")
PY

cases.purpose: Private-file receiver checks stdin with and without a final newline; CRLF input remains CRLF.
cases.script:
export BASHWALL_DEV_DIR=. BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 BASHWALL_FORCE_MESG=1
umask 000
printf 'prefix:' > receiver
chmod 666 receiver
printf 'first\nsecond' | write receiver
printf 'last\r\n' | write receiver
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
assert Path('receiver').read_bytes() == b'prefix:first\r\nsecond\r\nlast\r\n'
print('stdin newline bytes')
PY

cases.purpose: Capture control-byte rendering in an ordinary private receiver using the published careful-output rules, including NUL, DEL and high bytes. No terminal interprets these bytes.
cases.script:
export BASHWALL_DEV_DIR=. BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 BASHWALL_FORCE_MESG=1
umask 000
printf 'prefix:' > receiver
chmod 666 receiver
printf 'A\000B\177C\200D\tE\n' | write receiver
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
assert Path('receiver').read_bytes() == b'prefix:A^@B^?C\\200D\tE\r\n'
print('careful byte encoding')
PY

cases.purpose: A forced messages-disabled mode gate rejects a private regular-file receiver; missing relative targets also fail and leave existing data intact.
cases.script:
export BASHWALL_DEV_DIR=. BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1 BASHWALL_FORCE_MESG=1
umask 077
printf retained > receiver
if write receiver message; then a=0; else a=$?; fi
if write absent message; then b=0; else b=$?; fi
[[ $(<receiver) == retained ]]
printf '%s %s\n' "$a" "$b"

cases.purpose: Qualify real terminal/session banner, EOF marker and partial-write behavior.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r5: A short write cannot be forced on a tty or /dev/full from an unprivileged fixture. It needs syscall fault injection (seccomp user-notify or ptrace), and LD_PRELOAD does not apply to the static candidate.; r6: The candidate takes a TTY path, not a user name. util-linux write (bsdextrautils in the VM) needs a utmp login record, which requires root (utmp group) provisioning.
